patches.new: The approximation comes from assumptions 1 and 2 holding only for tiny pieces. Precisely, each piece is empty with probability $1-s/n+\epsilon_n$, where assumptions 1 and 2 say only that $\epsilon_n$ is negligible compared with $1/n$, that is, $n\epsilon_n\to0$. We show below that $n\log(1-x)\to-s$ for $x=s/n$; the argument uses only that $nx\to s$ and $x\to0$, and $x=s/n-\epsilon_n$ satisfies both. So the small errors $\epsilon_n$ do not accumulate over the $n$ pieces, and the approximation becomes exact as $n\to\infty$.
